recentItems.title: Sharing your smoking history could save your life | Rebecca Mattson | TEDxSanDiegoSalon
recentItems.description:
Have you ever under reported your smoking history, or left it out entirely, because you feared judgment or higher health insurance costs? You may think you’re protecting yourself, but withholding that information could mean risking your life.

Rebecca Mattson explores why people hesitate to share their full smoking history and why that conversation matters. She invites us to rethink what we tell our healthcare providers, and how we can make it easier for patients to speak openly, without shame.

An honest conversation could help protect your health, and save your life.

Connect with Rebecca: https://www.linkedin.com/in/mattsonsdsu?trk=contact-info

#SmokingHistory #PatientCare #HealthCommunication #TEDx #TEDxSanDiego #SDSU #moorescancercenter Dr. Rebecca Mattson, PhD, RN, is a nurse scientist and public health researcher at San Diego State University focused on improving population health through early disease detection. As a Co-Investigator on federally supported research, she leverages advanced artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) for the early detection of lung cancer.  Additionally, as a Principal Investigator partnering with a major healthcare system, Dr. Mattson utilizes Apple Health to explore how everyday health signals can reveal hidden disease risks. Her technology-driven research aims to bridge gaps between clinical healthcare and the home, transforming routine data into actionable opportunities for prevention and improved patient outcomes. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Urban design for the immune system | Miguel Reina-Campos | TEDxSanDiegoSalon
recentItems.description:
Would you be able to work in a broken, toxic environment? Your immune cells face a similar challenge.

When immune cells fail, tumors can progress. But fixing the cells themselves doesn’t always work. Miguel Reina-Campos explores a different question: What if the problem isn’t just the cells, but the tissue structures they move through? Could redesigning that environment help immune cells do their job?
Learn more about Reina Lab: https://www.reinalab.org/

#CancerResearch #Immunotherapy #ImmuneCells #TEDx #TEDxSanDiego #MooresCancerCenter #Cancer #environment #health #research Dr. Miguel Reina-Campos is an Assistant Professor at La Jolla Institute for Immunology, where he leads the Laboratory of Tissue Immune Networks. His lab studies how immune cells live and function inside tissues, with the goal of improving long-term protection against infections and cancer. He uses advanced technologies to map immune cells in tissue environments and understand how their location shapes immune defense. A biochemist by training, Dr. Reina-Campos obtained a B.Sc. from the Universitat de Barcelona, a M.Sc. from the Universitat Pompeu Fabra and the Scripps Research Institute, a Ph.D. in Biomedical Research at Sanford Burnham Prebys, and completed his Postdoctoral Fellowship in the laboratory of Dr. Goldrath at the University of California San Diego. Dr. Reina-Campos is a La Caixa Fellow, which is awarded by the King of Spain, and a Cancer Research Institute Fellow. Dr. Reina-Campos is the co-founder and board member of TCura Bioscience Inc. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Whole-body MRI, designed for women | Rebecca Rakow-Penner, MD, PhD | TEDxSanDiegoSalon
recentItems.description: Whole body MRI is exploding in popularity—but it was designed based on men's bodies, and not built to catch the diseases that matter most to women.  Dr. Rakow-Penner, a radiologist and MRI physicist reveals the gap in today's scans for women. Her call to action: stop retrofitting women into a man's blueprint, and build whole body MRI—head to toe—specifically for the patient actually on the table. @womensimager https://womensimaginglab.com    #health #Women #MRI #disease #UCSD #TEDxSanDiego #TEDx #MooresCancerResearch #scientist #Cancer #research Rebecca Rakow-Penner MD, PhD is tenured Associate Professor of Radiology and Bioengineering at University of California San Diego and a thought leader in women’s health. She has an undergraduate Engineering Sciences degree from Harvard, and master’s degree in Bioengineering from Caltech. Her PhD is in Biophysics from Stanford University where her research focused on breast MRI.  She also received her MD from Stanford and then completed her radiology residency and women’s imaging fellowship at UCSD.   She is a translational scientist and practicing radiologist in the breast and body imaging sections at UCSD.  She is the Director of the Women’s Imaging Lab and Co-Director of the Center for Translational Imaging.    Dr. Rakow-Penner has grant funding from NIH, industry, and private foundations for her ground-breaking research in breast, ovarian, and cervical cancer as well as benign female pelvis disease.  Her team is  working on AI approaches for the detection of female specific diseases. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: When Information Isn't Enough | Shiloh A. Williams, PhD, RN, NPD-BC, CNE | TEDxSanDiegoSalon
recentItems.description: What happens when healthcare gives patients all the right information but they still can’t use it when it matters most? Drawing from her experience as both a nurse researcher and a mother at her son’s ICU bedside, Dr. Shiloh Williams explores the critical gap between receiving health information and truly understanding it, and why understanding is critical in patient care. #healthcommunication https://pivotalempathy.com/  #Understandingishealthcare #PatientEngagement #Communication #Health #TEDxSanDiego #TEDx #Nurse #Research #Parent #Health Literacy Researcher #Nurse Educator#SDSU #moorescancercenter Dr. Shiloh A. Williams is a nurse educator, researcher, and health equity advocate whose work focuses on transforming how healthcare professionals communicate with patients. As an Assistant Professor of Nursing and co-director of the SDSU Imperial Valley RISE Center, she leads initiatives that address health literacy, chronic disease management, and care delivery in underserved communities. Her perspective is shaped not only by years in trauma and emergency care, but by a deeply personal experience as a mother navigating the healthcare system from the other side of the bedside. Through her work, she challenges the assumption that access to care is enough and argues that understanding is the true foundation of better health outcomes. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The virtual future of cancer research | Gege Qian | TEDxSanDiegoSalon
recentItems.description: What if, before choosing your cancer treatment, your doctor could test every option — not on you, but on a digital copy of your tumor living inside a computer? That's the promise of the virtual cell. Computational biologist Gege Qian explains how AI is learning to model living cells, what the future of the virtual cell could hold, and why it could change how we discover drugs and treat disease.  #Cancer #DigitalTwin, #AI #technology #VirtualCell #UCSD #TEDxSanDiego #TEDx #moorescancercenter #ComputationalBiologist Gege Qian is a computational oncologist and PhD candidate at UC San Diego, where she builds AI systems that map the inner architecture of living cells. Her work — published in Nature and under review at Science — uses machine learning to construct virtual cell models that reveal how cancer cells reorganize under chemotherapy, helping explain why patients relapse after treatment. A first-generation college student, Gege earned dual degrees from UC San Diego before completing her master's at Harvard Medical School. She has also worked as a venture capital fellow evaluating AI biotech startups and led biotech entrepreneurship initiatives that brokered partnerships with Roche. She believes the most important frontier in medicine is not a new drug — it is a new way of seeing cells. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Who gets into medicine and why it matters for patients | Mimi Hudson | TEDxSanDiegoSalon
recentItems.description: We talk a lot about who has access to healthcare. But who gets the chance to become the person providing it? Drawing from Mimi Hudson's own journey into healthcare, She explores how barriers to entering the healthcare workforce may be one of the most overlooked barriers to achieving health equity.  https://www.linkedin.com/in/mimihudson99/ IG:@mimi_bowman_ // #medicine #healthequity #premedprePA #TEDxSanDiego #TEDx #MooresCancerCenter #UCSD Mimi Hudson is a Clinical Research Coordinator with over five years of experience in healthcare. She earned her degree in Human Physiology from the University of Oregon and currently works at UCSD Health Moores Cancer Center as part of the Gynecologic Oncology Clinical Research team, where she supports clinical trials focused on advancing treatment options for women with cancer. She is particularly drawn to clinical research for the opportunities it creates for patients—expanding access to innovative therapies and providing care options that may not otherwise be available.  As an aspiring PA, Mimi is deeply committed to advancing equitable, inclusive healthcare. She is especially passionate about improving access, outcomes, and representation for women, communities of color, Indigenous populations, and other historically marginalized groups who continue to face systemic disparities in care. Her work is grounded in the belief that high-quality healthcare should be accessible to all. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Finding what stays true in medical research | Debashis Sahoo | TEDxSanDiegoSalon
recentItems.description:
What if the key to making science more reproducible is hiding in the patterns that never change? In this talk, Debashis Sahoo explores how AI can help us uncover invariant biological patterns hidden within the enormous complexity of human biology—and how these discoveries could reveal the laws that make science more reliable, medicine more precise, and knowledge more trustworthy.

Website: https://sites.google.com/view/debashis-sahoo
Twitter/X: @sahoo00
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/sahoodebashis/
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/debashis.sahoo

#ReproducibleScience #AIinBiology #FutureOfMedicine #TEDxSanDiego #TEDx #MooresCancerCenter #Bioinformatics #Boolean Analysis #UCSD #AI Debashis Sahoo is a joint Associate Professor of Computer Science and Engineering and Pediatrics at the University of California, San Diego. He earned his B.Tech. from the Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur, and his M.S. and Ph.D. from Stanford University. His research bridges artificial intelligence and biology, developing logical and AI-driven methods to uncover invariant biological rules and predict patient responses. His work has led to advances in cancer and translational research, including the identification of CDX2 as a predictive biomarker in colon cancer (NEJM 2016).  He is passionate about working at the intersection of disciplines and fostering collaborations among computational scientists, clinicians, and biologists to address real-world translational challenges. His group focuses on translating AI and logical modeling approaches into clinically actionable diagnostics and therapeutics. https://sites.google.com/view/debashis-sahoo This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. recentItems.title: Cancer as an ecosystem | Leslie Crews, PhD | TEDxSanDiegoSalon
recentItems.description:
What can endangered birds in New Zealand teach us about cancer? Drawing on insights from ecology, stem cell biology, and cancer research, Dr. Leslie Crews explores a new way of thinking about cancer: not simply as tumor cells to destroy, but as a disrupted ecosystem that may be restored. Through discoveries in blood cancer research, immune aging, and next-generation therapies, she shares how rebuilding cellular ecosystems could help shape the future of cancer treatment.
www.crews-lab.com
https://www.linkedin.com/in/lesliecrewsphd/
#bloodcancer #cancerecosystem #myeloma #TEDxSanDiego #TEDx #MooresCancerCenter #UCSD Dr. Leslie Crews is an Assistant Professor at UC San Diego and Co-Leader of the Hematologic Malignancies Research Program at the Moores Cancer Center. A third-generation native San Diegan, her first foray into scientific research was as a summer high school intern tasked with studying the behavior of fruit flies in a laboratory at the Salk Institute in La Jolla. She then trained at UCLA and UC San Diego in diverse biomedical research fields spanning neuroscience, eye disease, blood stem cell biology, geroscience, and cancer. Now her laboratory aims to uncover unifying biological circuitries that drive blood cancer regeneration and drug resistance. By targeting entire tumor ecosystems, her team is advancing new therapeutic strategies designed to reduce cancer burden while sparing healthy cells. Dr. Crews’ research is currently supported by an NCI R37 MERIT Award, a Blood Cancer United Scholar Award, and an American Society of Hematology Bridge Grant, among other national honors. www.crews-lab.com This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: “El Cielo sí existe” | Rochi Sporleder | TEDxSan Isidro
recentItems.description: El 24 de marzo de 2023 una infección por estreptococo pyogenes la llevó a un shock séptico que casi le cuesta la vida. Lo que vino después, fue un camino de 500 días de internación, 50 cirugías y un proceso de rehabilitación en el que tuvo que reaprender a tragar, a escribir, a vestirse. Hoy Rochi está en silla de ruedas. Es una sobreviviente que decidió convertir esa experiencia límite en un mensaje de resiliencia con una autenticidad y fortaleza admirables recordándonos que incluso en los momentos más difíciles es posible encontrar esperanza, sentido y una nueva manera de vivir. Abogada, psicóloga y speaker motivacional This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: 啟德以外的香港足球：由聯賽開始撐起本地波 | Philip Chan | TEDxLion Rock
recentItems.description:
啟德主場館落成後，港足比賽破紀錄獲逾47,000人入場支持，熱鬧氣氛令人振奮。然而，啟德以外的球賽是同樣光景嗎？香港足球先生陳肇鈞帶我們一探本地波實況，並談及他一路走來的省思。 陳肇鈞Philip Chan 是中國香港足球隊代表，也是首位遠赴巴西受訓的香港青年球員。他在2023/24球季成為「四料香港足球先生」，囊括多個獎項。

球場內外，逆境波總少不了，Philip將與我們分享他作為本地運動員走過的高山低谷，以及一路走來的各種觀察省思。 This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: “Renacer de mis cenizas” | Tatiana Ruiz | TEDxSan Isidro
recentItems.description: Tatiana comparte un mensaje esperanzador sobre la posibilidad de transformar la adversidad en una oportunidad para volver a elegir la vida. Desde una experiencia marcada por el dolor, la desesperación y el haber tocado fondo, invita a reflexionar sobre la importancia de recuperar el control, construir vínculos saludables y descubrir en el amor una fuerza capaz de impulsar los cambios que necesitamos. Su charla es una invitación a no bajar los brazos y a recordar que siempre estamos a tiempo de cambiar, reconstruirnos y volver a empezar. Espartana en libertad y entrenadora de “Las Vencedoras” equipo de rugby de mujeres privadas de su libertad del Complejo Ezeiza. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: 福地上的 Gen Z：創造福地由關心鄰里開始 | Yoyo Ng | TEDxLion Rock
recentItems.description:
香港成長的人都曾聽過這句話：「香港是一片福地。」十年前，TEDxKowloon 亦以此為題舉行過一場演講。十年後的今日，香港社工系學生吳樂瑤向我們講解她對「福地」的詮釋，強調香港是否福地，取決於心態與行動。 Yoyo 為 H-Infinity 社會文化實踐計劃中的「曾經的香港製造：港式叉燒的前世今生」核心成員之一，現於香港中文大學社會工作學系攻讀其社會科學學士學位。她關注社區發展、本地文化及義工服務，熱衷與社會企業合作推動社區項目，並對社區營造、跨代共融及政策倡議抱有濃厚興趣。

Yoyo is one of the core members of the H-Infinity Social and Cultural Practice Programme ‘Once made in Hong Kong: Char Siu then and now’. She is currently pursuing a BSSc degree in the Department of Social Work, CUHK. Passionate about community development, local culture, and volunteerism, Yoyo actively collaborates with social enterprises to implement community projects. Her interests also extend to community building, intergenerational inclusion, and policy advocacy, through which she hopes to contribute to a more connected and compassionate society. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
